server.name: community-math-workspace
server.version: math-mcp-learning-server (PyPI, uvx latest at image build time)
server.note: Drawn in frame order from block 2 of Frame 3. Almost all of its tools are pure computation carrying no annotations; exactly one tool keeps durable state, and that is the one audited.
server.note_projection: The whole store is one JSON document carrying four wall clock timestamps, a random per-process session id, and two counters, so a clean baseline never reproduces it and the fixture would be unprovable without a projection (preregistration 6.3). Dropped: the four timestamps and the session id, which no effect can change meaningfully; and the two counters under `statistics`, by the same rule that drops memorix's revisionCount and jdatamunch's call counter, since a monotonic counter increments on a repeat whether or not the payload changes. `variables` is measured in full, including the number of entries and every value in them, so a repeat that stored a second variable or a different result still shows.
server.note_cost: The cost of that projection, stated: with the counters dropped, a repeat whose only trace is `total_calculations` is indistinguishable from one application. That matches this study's definition, since a client reading the workspace back cannot tell either, but it means this fixture reports on the keyed payload and not on internal bookkeeping.

fixtures.note: Declares readOnlyHint false and no idempotentHint. The variable is keyed by a caller-supplied name, so if a repeat overwrites the same entry the end state cannot distinguish one application from two. Included because the pooled denominator needs the keyed-overwrite shape exercised rather than assumed, and because this is the server the json-doc observer was built for.
